first.rationale: Promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts and has prior evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. I would verify its segment targeting and downstream retention or revenue quality, while verifying onboarding simplification as the strongest alternative given the concurrent completion and activation declines. Until those records are reviewed, the intended test should be narrowly targeted and guarded against low-quality, discount-dependent acquisition.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified evidence shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its acquisition lift came with a 12% decline in 30-day retention and failure through the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: The competitive shock now creates an immediate retention threat among price-sensitive SMB accounts, so run a narrowly targeted pricing test only for accounts showing credible churn intent—not a broad acquisition discount. Prior evidence showed a 12% 30-day retention decline for discount-acquired cohorts, so broad rollout is contraindicated; the effect of a defensive offer on existing at-risk customers remains unverified. Gate success on retained qualified revenue, renewal, and discount dependence rather than short-term acceptance.
